tasks.short: Monitor food intake and weight and report actual changes

steps.what: Review the identified patient's existing food-intake and weight records and dietitian monitoring instructions
inputs: verified patient identity
care-team recorded intake and weight entries with dates, units and sources
dietitian-issued monitoring instructions
outputs: checked prior intake and weight context

steps.what: Observe and monitor actual patient food intake and obtain or verify actual body weight within the assigned monitoring work
inputs: checked prior intake and weight context
actual patient, meal intake and weight observation
outputs: actual intake and weight observations with dates and uncertainties

steps.what: Enter actual food-intake and body-weight observations, source, units and missing or uncertain values
inputs: actual intake and weight observations with dates and uncertainties
verified patient identity
outputs: complete draft actual intake and weight entries

steps.what: Assess and write actual changes, progress and dietary problems for the dietitian without inferring normality from missing data
inputs: complete draft actual intake and weight entries
checked prior intake and weight context
actual patient observations and dietary concerns
outputs: technician-written change, progress and dietary-problem findings

steps.what: Prepare the complete dietitian report from actual entries and technician-written findings with the intended dietitian recipient
inputs: complete draft actual intake and weight entries
technician-written change, progress and dietary-problem findings
assigned dietitian recipient from the care record
outputs: complete intake, weight and dietary-problem report packet

steps.what: Verify and approve the final actual entries, report and named dietitian recipient
inputs: complete intake, weight and dietary-problem report packet
outputs: approved monitoring report packet v1

steps.what: Save the approved monitoring entries and report as one patient monitoring record in the same care system
inputs: approved monitoring report packet v1
outputs: stored actual patient monitoring record

steps.what: Send the approved report to the assigned internal dietitian
inputs: approved monitoring report packet v1
stored actual patient monitoring record
outputs: delivered actual monitoring report

tasks.design: Configure the {OPS_SYSTEM} patient monitoring view, dated observation form and fixed report layout. The technician obtains and enters actual observations, writes the meaningful changes and problems, then checks the assembled final report before separate storage and delivery to the dietitian.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reference navigation, form layout and report assembly can add work around actual patient observation and assessment.
tasks.enabler_now: Native dated fields and fixed report sections can reuse captured facts without interpreting dietary progress.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete intake observations and variable weight measurement conditions require human interpretation and clarification.
tasks.human_edge: Notice a dietary problem that the numeric trend alone does not explain.

ambition.what: No additional clinical decision authority is assumed.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-6 for patient-data access and care-team consultation on recording changes

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: care systems can display dated observations and assemble fixed reports from actual structured entries and human-written findings.

assumptions: Boundary includes observation, actual record capture, assessment and reporting to the dietitian. Clinical programme decisions and dietitian review are other-role work outside the focal denominator and receive no saving.

Care-team existing entries include patient id, date, measure, unit and source; the dietitian supplies monitoring instructions. s2 obtains actual new observations and s3 retains fifteen hours for entry, uncertainty and correction. No device integration, transcript or free structured capture is assumed.
s4 explicitly writes change and problem findings before s5 assembles them verbatim with the observation table. Native configuration first; no model infers a problem or invents a missing measurement.
Shares and reductions are provisional scenarios, not measured baselines. No paper or rekey history is asserted. Same-system save and short internal send remain fully retained.
Approval binds this single patient's exact entries, report and recipient; any edit requires renewed approval. Urgent patient concerns follow existing human procedures and earn no saving here.
unknowns: Current native monitoring and report functionality
Actual form navigation and report assembly effort
research_questions: Can every reported value be traced to an actual dated observation and source?
Does the form preserve unknown intake rather than converting it to zero?

already_counted.description: Capture and check actual monitoring observations
Check fixed report assembly and patient identity

incremental.description: Maintain observation fields, report layout and dietitian-routing mappings

approvals.approved_version: approved monitoring report packet v1 with exact patient entries and report; edits void approval
approved monitoring report packet v1 including named dietitian recipient; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross 17.5 minus 1 upkeep gives 16.5. High allows 4.5 additional hours correcting uncertain observation references; low applies when native forms and reports already cover this work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assess dietary histories to help plan nutritional programmes

steps.what: Review the individual's existing dietary information and the supervising dietitian's assessment guidance
inputs: verified individual identity and existing dietary records
dietitian-issued assessment guidance and role boundary
outputs: checked dietary assessment context

steps.what: Obtain the individual's actual dietary history through questions, examples and clarification
inputs: checked dietary assessment context
actual individual account and available supporting information
outputs: actual dietary-history account with uncertainties and relevant circumstances

steps.what: Record the actual dietary history, source attribution, examples and uncertain or missing information
inputs: actual dietary-history account with uncertainties and relevant circumstances
checked dietary assessment context
outputs: complete draft actual dietary history

steps.what: Evaluate the actual dietary history and other available information in the nutritional assessment within the technician's assigned scope
inputs: complete draft actual dietary history
checked dietary assessment context
outputs: technician-formed nutritional assessment and unresolved questions

steps.what: Write the programme-planning contribution from the assessment, with proposed priorities and questions for dietitian review
inputs: technician-formed nutritional assessment and unresolved questions
dietitian-issued assessment guidance and role boundary
outputs: complete nutritional assessment and programme-planning contribution

steps.what: Check the final history, assessment and planning contribution and approve their internal record version
inputs: complete nutritional assessment and programme-planning contribution
complete draft actual dietary history
outputs: approved assessment record packet v1

steps.what: Save the approved history, assessment and planning contribution as one internal assessment record
inputs: approved assessment record packet v1
outputs: stored actual nutritional assessment and planning contribution

tasks.design: Configure an existing-information view and dietary-history form in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, reusing verified identity and existing reference fields. The technician conducts the history, records actual meaning, evaluates it and writes the programme-planning contribution before approving its record version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reference lookup and repeated case metadata can add effort around obtaining and evaluating a dietary history.
tasks.enabler_now: Native forms can reuse known identity and reference fields without generating a patient's history or nutritional assessment.
tasks.still_hard: Recall, context, uncertainty and individual needs require careful questioning and assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when an apparently precise account is incomplete and ask a useful follow-up question.

ambition.what: No expanded clinical authority is assumed.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-5 for dietary records and care-team consultation about changed forms

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: structured care forms can reuse verified identity and existing references while people capture actual histories and assessments.

assumptions: Boundary includes obtaining and evaluating history and writing a nutritional programme-planning contribution under dietitian supervision. The technician's record approval does not authorise a clinical programme beyond the assigned scope; dietitian decision work is separate and receives no saving.

The care record supplies identity and dated existing information; the dietitian supplies guidance. s2 obtains the actual account and s3 retains twelve hours for substantive capture, attribution and uncertainty. No transcript, automatic diagnosis or freely structured conversation output is assumed.
Native configuration first. Prefill reuses only known case metadata; all assessment and programme-planning judgement stays fully retained. There is no automatic dietitian send or plan activation.
Shares and reductions are provisional scenarios, not measured baselines. Same-system saving remains fully retained; if native forms already reuse these fields, the gain is zero.
unknowns: Existing assessment form and permitted technician scope
research_questions: Does the history form preserve attributed and uncertain statements?
Does prefill reduce effort without changing assessment meaning?

already_counted.description: Capture and check the actual dietary history and uncertainty

incremental.description: Maintain dietary-history form references and fields

approvals.approved_version: approved assessment record packet v1 including exact history, assessment and contribution; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross 8 minus 0.5 upkeep gives 7.5. High allows 2.5 additional hours checking uncertain source references; low applies when existing native views and forms already cover the work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Determine group food quantities and prepare a major meal

steps.what: Check the authorised recipes, actual group meal count and established dietary requirements for the major meal
inputs: kitchen-owner approved recipe versions with base yield and ingredient quantities
meal-order owner actual portions by authorised meal variant and service time
outputs: checked meal preparation inputs

steps.what: Determine group food quantities by scaling each authorised recipe's ingredient amounts to the checked portions
inputs: checked meal preparation inputs
outputs: calculated ingredient quantities by authorised recipe variant with units

steps.what: Check the quantity plan against actual ingredients, recipe applicability and established dietary requirements before preparation
inputs: calculated ingredient quantities by authorised recipe variant with units
actual ingredients and kitchen conditions
checked meal preparation inputs
outputs: technician-checked meal preparation quantities and unresolved discrepancies

steps.what: Prepare the major meal following the authorised recipes and checked group food quantities, resolving discrepancies through existing supervision
inputs: technician-checked meal preparation quantities and unresolved discrepancies
actual kitchen ingredients, equipment and authorised recipes
outputs: actual major meal prepared within established instructions

tasks.design: Configure the {OPS_SYSTEM} recipe-scaling function to use checked actual meal counts and authorised recipes from the {DOCS}. The technician checks the resulting quantities against dietary requirements and actual ingredients, then prepares the meal; software neither changes a recipe nor substitutes an ingredient.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated portion lookup and proportional arithmetic can add effort before physical cooking.
tasks.enabler_now: Native recipe scaling can multiply explicit quantities and preserve variant and unit references without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Actual ingredients, differing recipe behaviour at scale and established dietary requirements need kitchen judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a mathematically scaled quantity is unsuitable for the actual preparation conditions.

ambition.what: Recalculate an authorised meal variant's quantities when the confirmed portion count changes.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-4 for recipe and meal-count access and kitchen consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: recipe systems can proportionally scale approved ingredient quantities to explicit portion counts with unit checks.

assumptions: Boundary includes checked meal inputs, determining quantities and actual preparation. Serving and any separate food-safety or production records remain governed by existing work and earn no saving here; this proposal introduces no hidden record or send.

Kitchen owners supply recipe id, version, base yield, ingredient id, amount and unit; meal-order owners supply actual portions by authorised variant. s1 retains manual checking and missing-count resolution, not a free new structured-count collection process.
Native scaling first. s2 retains 4.5 hours for calculation and unit checks. New recipe or dietary decisions, substitutions, kitchen setup and all physical preparation remain human and fully retained.

Shares and reductions are provisional scenarios, not measured baselines. Existing system runtime earns no labour saving; no paper or manual rekey history is asserted. If native scaling already works, this design's gain is zero.
The quantity output is a temporary planning view, not a committed recipe change or automatic kitchen instruction. No persistent save or transmission is proposed.
unknowns: Existing recipe scaling and count integration
Actual time spent finding portions and calculating quantities
research_questions: Can a reviewed meal be reproduced with explicit variant, yield and unit references?
Does a change in portions expose any recipe that cannot simply scale proportionally?

already_counted.description: Check scaled amounts, yield and units

incremental.description: Maintain approved recipe-to-variant mappings and scaling checks

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross 16.5 minus 1 upkeep gives 15.5. High allows 4.5 additional hours checking count and scaling exceptions; low applies where existing native recipe functions already cover the work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Supervise food production or service and assist dietitian planning

steps.what: Review the current food production or service plan, actual meal demand and the dietitian's established requirements
inputs: kitchen-owner current production or service plan and actual status
meal-order owner actual demand
dietitian-issued requirements and supervision priorities
outputs: checked food-service supervision context

steps.what: Supervise actual food production or service and observe compliance with the established plan and requirements
inputs: checked food-service supervision context
actual food production or service and staff activity
outputs: actual food-service supervision findings and issues

steps.what: Clarify actual issues with staff and assist dietitians or nutritionists in food-service supervision or planning decisions
inputs: actual food-service supervision findings and issues
actual staff and supervising dietitian responses
outputs: actual supervisory clarifications and technician planning contribution

steps.what: Record actual supervision findings, clarifications and planning contribution in the existing food-service record
inputs: actual food-service supervision findings and issues
actual supervisory clarifications and technician planning contribution
checked food-service supervision context
outputs: complete actual food-service supervision note

steps.what: Check and approve the final actual supervision note without treating suggestions as authorised plan changes
inputs: complete actual food-service supervision note
outputs: approved food-service supervision note v1

steps.what: Save the approved note in the same internal food-service supervision record
inputs: approved food-service supervision note v1
outputs: stored actual food-service supervision note

tasks.design: Configure the {OPS_SYSTEM} supervision view to link current food-service plans and {DOCS} requirements, then reuse known service identifiers in the existing note form. The technician observes the actual work, assists the dietitian through discussion and records actual findings before approving and saving the note.
tasks.previous_blocker: Locating current plans and repeating service metadata can add effort around direct supervision.
tasks.enabler_now: Native linked views and forms can reuse existing references without inferring food-service completion or authorising a dietary change.
tasks.still_hard: Actual service quality, staff coordination and unexpected dietary issues require human supervision.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise a practical mismatch between the plan and what is actually being prepared or served.

ambition.what: No additional nutritional or management authority is assumed.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-5 for food-service records and staff consultation if attribution changes

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: linked operational views and forms can reuse service-plan references while people capture actual supervision findings.

assumptions: Boundary covers one assigned production or service supervision episode, associated planning assistance and its existing note. Other staff food preparation and dietitian decisions are outside the focal denominator and receive no saving.

Kitchen owners supply plan id, version and already recorded actual status; meal-order owners supply demand; dietitians supply established requirements. Missing status is checked manually in s1/s2, not imposed as free new reporting on others.

s4 retains seven hours for actual findings, clarifications and planning contribution capture. Only known service and plan references can be reused. Native configuration first; no automatic judgement or changed plan is produced.

Shares and reductions are provisional scenarios, not measured baselines. Where no supervision note exists, remeasure the task rather than inventing paperwork savings. Same-system save remains fully retained.
Overlap with meal preparation and patient monitoring records must be reconciled before roll-up; no shared id is used for merely related work.
unknowns: Actual supervision note practice and current plan links
research_questions: Does the view distinguish actual status from planned production?
Does the note preserve the difference between a planning suggestion and an approved change?

already_counted.description: Capture and check actual supervision findings and planning contribution

incremental.description: Maintain service-plan links and note form fields

approvals.approved_version: approved food-service supervision note v1; edits require s5 again

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross 9 minus 0.5 upkeep gives 8.5. High allows 2.5 extra hours resolving outdated plan references; low applies where native views and form links already cover this work.

role.altitude: The technician spends less time finding references and assembling quantities or records while retaining patient conversations, practical food preparation, assessment and supervision under a dietitian.
skills_to_grow: Preserve observation dates, units and uncertainty
Check recipe scaling against authorised variants
Distinguish planning contributions from clinical authority
role.ambitious_version: Give the supervising dietitian clear actual observations and transparent food-service quantities without replacing patient contact or kitchen judgement.
